samples.text:
Nowadays, many young people continue to live with their parents after they finish their studies. This situation has some advantages and disadvantages for both the young adults and their parents.

For young adults, the biggest advantage is money. Rent is very expensive in most cities, so if they live at home they can save a big part of their salary. Later they can use this money to buy their own house or car. Also, they do not have to do all the housework alone, because the mother often cook and clean for the family. For parents, it can also be good. They can spend more time with their children and they do not feel lonely, especially if they are old. Moreover, the children can help them with shopping or with technology, for example using a smartphone.

However, there are also some disadvantages. Young adults who stay at home may not become independent. They do not learn how to pay bills, manage their own money or solve problems by themself. They also have less privacy, and sometimes they cannot invite friends to the house. For the parents, the problem is that they have to pay more for food and electricity, and they cannot enjoy their free time after retirement. In addition, there can be many arguments, because parents and children have different lifestyle and opinions.

In conclusion, living together helps young adults to save money and gives the parents company. But it can also stop young people from becoming independent and cause conflicts in the family. I think it is fine for a short time, but young people should moves out when they are ready.
samples.why: Covers both groups · relevant ideas but explanation is brief and general · simple, mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary with some awkward collocation · agreement and word-form errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
It is increasingly common for young people to remain in the family home after completing their education, rather than moving into a place of their own. This arrangement has both benefits and drawbacks, not only for the young adults themselves but also for their parents.

For young adults, the most significant advantage is financial. With rents and property prices rising in many cities, living with parents allows them to save money for a deposit on a home or to pay off student loans more quickly. It can also provide emotional support during a stressful period, such as the search for a first job. Parents, too, can benefit. Many enjoy the continued companionship of their children, and as they grow older, having an adult son or daughter at home means there is someone to help with household tasks, shopping or unexpected health problems.

On the other hand, the arrangement has clear disadvantages. Young people who stay at home for too long may delay developing important life skills, such as budgeting, cooking and managing a household, and they may become overly dependent on their parents. A lack of privacy and personal space can also make it harder for them to build independent social lives. For parents, supporting an adult child can put pressure on their finances just when they are planning for retirement. Moreover, disagreements over household rules, chores or lifestyle are common when two adult generations share the same space, and these tensions can damage family relationships.

In conclusion, living together can offer young adults financial security and give parents company and practical help. However, it may also slow the development of independence and create financial and emotional strains on both sides. Ideally, such arrangement should be temporary and based on clear agreements about responsibilities.
samples.why: Addresses both sides for both groups · ideas extended with relevant examples, some generalisation · clear central topic in each paragraph · good collocation (pay off loans, life skills) · mostly error-free, one article slip.

samples.text:
In many societies, the age at which young people leave the family home is steadily rising, with growing numbers remaining with their parents well after they have completed their education. This trend carries a mixture of advantages and disadvantages for both generations, and its overall impact depends heavily on how the arrangement is managed.

For young adults, the benefits are largely economic. At a time when housing costs absorb an ever-larger proportion of starting salaries, living at home enables graduates to build savings, repay debts and accept lower-paid but career-enhancing positions that they could not otherwise afford. The family home can also serve as a safety net during an uncertain transition into working life. Parents may gain as well: the presence of an adult child can provide companionship, particularly for those who live alone, and practical assistance with everything from home repairs to navigating online services. In some cultures, multigenerational living is valued in its own right as a way of preserving close family ties.

The disadvantages, however, are equally real. Remaining under the parental roof can postpone the development of self-reliance, since many of the responsibilities that force young people to mature, such as paying rent and running a household, are absorbed by others. Limited privacy may also constrain their social lives. For parents, the arrangement can mean extra expense and a delayed opportunity to enjoy the freedom they may have anticipated once their children had grown up. Perhaps most significantly, adults with different routines and expectations sharing a home can generate friction, and unresolved tensions may strain relationships that would otherwise be harmonious.

In conclusion, continued co-residence offers young adults financial breathing space and parents companionship and support, but it risks delaying independence and generating conflict. The arrangement tends to work best when it is treated as a temporary stage, with clear expectations on both sides.
samples.why: Fully addresses all parts for both generations · well-developed, relevant ideas in logical sequence · skilful cohesion · wide, precise vocabulary (safety net, self-reliance, co-residence) · wide range of error-free structures.
